FOREWORD This Indian Standard ( Part 1 ) was adopted by the Bureau of Indian Standards, after the draft finalized by the Methods of Chemical Analysis of Ferrous Metals Sectional Committee had been approved by the Metallurgical Engineering Division Council. IS 1559 : 1961 `Methods of chemical analysis of ferroalloys' covers the chemical analysis of different ferroferrochromium, ferromanganese and speigeleisen, silicomanganese, ferroalloys, namely, ferrosilicon, ferrovanadium and ferrotungesten. While reviewing this ferrophosphorus, ferrotitanium, molybdenum, standard, the Sectional Committee had decided that a separate `series for each ferroalloy be prepared. Accordingly, IS 1559 in its various parts was published for the chemical analysis of ferrosilicon. The chemical analysis of ferromolybdenum is covered in a series of parts of IS1 2614. The chemical analysis of ferrochromium is covered in a series of parts of this standard. With the publication of these parts the analysis of relevant constitueut prescribed for ferrochromium in IS 1559 : 1961 will be superseded, This part covers the method for determination of silicon in high carbon ferrochromium. The other parts are: Part 2 Determination Part 3 Determination Part 4 Determination Part 5 Determination Part 6 Determination Part 7 Determination Part 8 Determination In this revision of silicon in low carbon of phosphorus of total sulphur of chromium of chromium of nitrogen of carbon ferrochromium ferrochromium ferrochromium ferrochromium ferrochromium ferrochromium ferrochromium has been updated. in low carbon in high carbon in low carbon

SAMPLING prepared in

`The sample shall be drawn and accordance with IS 1472 : 1977. 4 QUALITY OF REAGENTS

sodium peroxide and 2 g of anhydrous sodirun carbonate. Mix well and cover with 2 g of sodium peroxide. Fuse the content carefully over the dull flame of Meeker burner or in a muffle furnace at a temperature 5509 to 600%. Care should be taken not to raise the temperature rapidly as to cause spattering. When the mass is molten, a slight rotary motion is imparted to the crucible to stir up any unattacked particles of alloy on t.hc bottom or sides. The temperature is to be increased to a bright redness for a minute just before completion of fusion. If followed carefully, a very quite fusion without any spattering will result. After the crucible has cooled, slowly drop the crucible with its solidified melt in 50 ml ob' cold water in a 500 ml polytetrafluroethylene ( PTFE ) beaker and cover with PTFE cove-~glass. When the reaction has subsided take out crucible and wash with warm hydrochloric acid ( 10 percent ) and then with water collecting all the washings in the same PTFE beaker. 5.3.2 Acidify the extract ( 5.3.1 ) by addir.g 50 ml of hydrochloric acid and then transfer the solution to a 500 ml glass beaker, evaporate to almost syrupy stage and add 30 ml of perchloric acid and keep the beaker on hot plate until white perchloric acid fumes are refluxed for 15 minutes.
NOTE - The dehydration of the silica in high carbon ferrochromium can be carried out even by sulphuric acid, but the difficulties are frequently encountered drw to the insolubility of basic chromic salts due to thl: presence of high chromium content of the alloy. By fuming with perchloric acid for dehydration, this sort uf difficulty will not occur as perchloratcs are easily soluble even in cold water.
